extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Coming Up shows films as posters, three across each day, and marks the chosen TV episode as the Apple TV app does. - Discover remembers your filters: they are kept on your profile, the same as in tofa's web app. - Turning a Discover filter on or off no longer moves the focus to the top bar. - Who's watching has a profile selected straight away, also on the first start after Kodi opens. - After updating, tofa asks once more to install its fonts.

extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Discover follows the Apple TV app: For You, Trending, Coming Up, Best Of, Universes and Genres. Coming Up is a week planner for TV shows and films, one column per day; Universes lists every film and TV universe; a genre opens its own page, which you can follow. - Home has a new row, Continue the saga, under Continue Watching: the film and TV universes you are part way through, each with the next title to watch. Select one to see the whole universe in story or release order. A title's page shows the universe it belongs to, with its place in it, and Down on a universe lists every title by chapter. - A universe's page can request what your library is missing, for the whole universe or one chapter, if your server has Radarr or Sonarr. - A title you don't have shows Seen it and Not interested on its page; both are marked with a filled icon once set. - Card menus list their choices in the Apple TV app's order, and Not interested takes the card off the row straight away. - On a title page, the options menu of More Like This, More to Discover and a collection's titles now does what it offers: Watchlist and Mark as Watched work there, and Seen it and Not interested appear where they apply. - A film resumes the edition you were watching last, wherever you open it from, not the first one listed. - Browse shows your libraries in a row of their own, above Watchlist, History, Collections and Surprise me. - Back on Browse, Discover, Search or Settings now returns to Home, to the card you were on. - Settings > Appearance has Missing episodes: Automatic, Always show or Never show. - Playback Options lists each quality as 1080p, 720p and so on, with the rate the server will actually send. - After updating, tofa asks once more to install its fonts.

extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Needs tofa media server 0.12.0 or newer. An older server still works, but you are told once per session that some screens may be incomplete. - Mark a title Seen it or Not interested from its options menu: on Discover, on Suggested for You, and on a title you don't have. - Browse opens on Movies, TV Shows and Other, as tofa groups your libraries, instead of one tile per library. - A person's page lists their whole filmography at once, including the films in your library that they directed or wrote. - Show pages follow your profile's Missing episodes setting in tofa: Automatic, Always show or Never show. - Turning subtitles on skips commentary and short forced tracks when a full one is there, and the track list labels forced and commentary tracks.

extension.summary: Fonts for the tofa for Kodi add-on
extension.description:
The typefaces the tofa for Kodi add-on draws its own screens in: Inter Tight, Roboto Mono and the Lucide icon set.
Installed automatically as a dependency of tofa for Kodi. It provides font files and nothing else: no screens, no settings, and nothing runs. It is not useful on its own.
Kodi looks inside enabled font resources for any font file it cannot find in the active skin, so tofa's screens can name these files without a copy of them being placed in the skin.
